scene_summary: A worn paper plate with torn deckled borders holds a smeared billiards-room scene. The dominant source-bearing gesture is a long emerald fuselage-like band crossing the upper-middle, interrupted by ripped vertical seams, pale ceiling scratches, a greenhouse-like pasted patch at upper right, small table glints, and right-side monochrome figures compressed into a damaged aperture.
usable_surfaces: long emerald horizontal smear across the upper-middle
pale torn greenhouse-like patch at upper right
vertical ripped paper seam left of center
diagonal ceiling scratches in the upper field
right-side figure aperture and dark pasted edge
tiny white glints on the pool-table felt
lower-left torn paper notch and black void
yellow and orange billiard color nodes

detected_objects.label: hero emerald fuselage tear
detected_objects.visual_evidence: A long green smeared band runs nearly the full width, with a bright pale lower edge and darker emerald body, visibly torn and abraded like a fuselage rupture.

detected_objects.label: hero procedural creature smear
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Below the green band at left is a murky black-green, creature-like smear with smoky limbs, chair-like arcs, and rubbed animation residue embedded in the wall and lower table edge.

detected_objects.label: cream greenhouse border
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Upper right contains a cream-white pasted rectangle under a green cap, with faded diagonal greenhouse-like lines and paper grain distinct from the surrounding wall.

detected_objects.label: trench-line ceiling scratch
detected_objects.visual_evidence: A pale diagonal scratch arcs from the upper center-right down toward the right wall, with repeated fine trench-map-like incisions crossing the ceiling surface.

detected_objects.label: hepburn-crowd aperture
detected_objects.visual_evidence: The right side compresses standing human figures into a torn monochrome-dark aperture, bounded by rubbed white scratches and the ragged paper edge.

detected_objects.label: arts-index paper notch
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Lower left has a torn pale-to-black paper notch with scan-grain, curled edge, and dark void beneath, suitable as a catalog/index remnant.

detected_objects.label: Secondary Source Anchor
detected_objects.visual_evidence: The turquoise billiards table is the clearest lower source surface, a broad trapezoidal plane carrying the player's gesture, balls, scratches, and small white glints.

detected_objects.label: Color Node
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Two saturated billiard balls puncture the muted plate: a yellow node at lower left of the felt and an orange node nearer center-left.

detected_objects.label: Color Node
detected_objects.visual_evidence: Planned source surface fallback used because plate inspection returned fewer mapped objects than source bindings.

complexity_assessment.rationale: The plate has strong source-bearing anchors and expressive torn edges, but it is visually dense: the fuselage smear, table plane, right figure aperture, vertical rips, and paper border all compete. Still usable because the major marks remain legible and separable.

mapping_note: Package assembly filled unmapped source pockets from planned artifact surfaces because plate inspection returned too few detected objects.
